chunks: And from him, from Fadala, from Mu'awiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no harm in killing ants and lice in the Haram (sanctuary), and there is no harm in killing head lice in the Haram."

And whatever was permissible for the Muhsil (one not in Ihram) to kill in the Haram, that is also permissible for the Muhrim (one in Ihram) to kill, from camels, cattle, sheep, and other than that. It was narrated.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.لِلْمُحِلِّ: For the one not in Ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim in Ihram kill ants or lice in the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between minor pests and larger livestock within the Haram boundaries, affirming that the prohibition on killing specific animals does not extend to insects like ants and lice for both the Muhrim and Muhsil. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (yusr) in ritual purity and sanctuary laws, noting that while larger animals require specific conditions, small pests are exempt from the stricter Ihram restrictions. This ruling is foundational for understanding the nuances of *kaffarah* (expiation) when a pilgrim inadvertently kills creatures in the sacred precincts.
